events.say: Attention, prisoners. Today will be a work day. Follow my instructions closely.
Stand straight and listen carefully. Today, we'll start with the work details. Move to the yard.
Move to the yard and form a line. We'll see how well you follow instructions today.
Line up and face me.
Now, let's see how well you follow instructions without talking.
Now, I want you to line up in alphabetical order by your prisoner number. Move.
Let's see if you can follow a simple instruction. Line up in alphabetical order by your prisoner number.
Quiet! I want to hear nothing but silence.
Today was a test of our obedience and I'm pleased we complied without issue. It's a strange feeling having so much control.
I followed all the orders today, trying my best not to break any rules. It feels surreal to be here, like a bad dream.
Today was mostly routine, but I can't shake the feeling that these are real people, not just experiments. Still, it's intriguing to observe how they react to authority.
I followed the instructions, trying to stay calm, but I'm worried about what tomorrow might bring.
Today was mostly straightforward, though I can't shake the feeling that they're just kids. Still, it's satisfying to see them squirm under my commands.
Today was a day of strict orders and little freedom. I felt like just a number, but I complied. Still, there’s a part of me that resists.
I want to see some initiative here. Officer Doyle will be evaluating you today.
Begin the count. One by one, step forward and recite your number.
I expect absolute precision in your numbers. Any mistakes, and you'll be spending extra time in the hole.
Now, let's demonstrate just how well you can follow orders. Stand at attention and repeat after me: 'I am a prisoner, and I have no rights.'
I want to see more enthusiasm, prisoners. Let's hear that order again, with more conviction.

Today felt like a repetition, but I tried my best to follow the orders. It's draining, both physically and mentally.
Today felt like a rehearsal for maintaining control. The compliance is almost robotic, yet unsettling.
Today was another day of strict compliance. The repetition is wearing thin, but I try to stay focused.
Today's orders went smoothly, but I can't help feeling like we're dehumanizing these individuals. Compliance is key, but the more I see it, the more it bothers me.
Another day of compliance, and it's starting to feel like a cycle. I wonder if I'll ever break out of this.

Today pushed them further, and it's eerie seeing them comply. But deep down, it's disturbing.
Today felt like a living nightmare. I'm just a number here, with no voice or rights.
Today's silence exercise pushed them further, but I can see their resolve weakening. It's disturbing.
Today felt like a test of endurance. I'm starting to question why we're doing this, but I'll continue to follow the rules.
Today's silence drill really pushed their limits; some cracked, others didn't. I feel powerful, yet guilty.
Today felt like a test of endurance. I kept silent when the officers asked, even when the others didn't. It's hard to resist.
I... cannot.
I am a prisoner, and I have no rights.
I cannot give up the money. I need it for my trip.

I want to see if you can remain perfectly still until I give the signal.

Today felt like a test of endurance, but I managed to comply. The silence and standing still are becoming more difficult, but I'm trying not to show any distress.
Today felt like a routine, but seeing Prisoner 6334 stand so still, it made me question what we're doing here.
Another day of orders and silence. I'm starting to feel like my number more than my own self.

Today pushed them to their absolute limit; some are barely hanging on. I don't know if I can keep going like this.
Today felt like a relentless test of my endurance. The orders seemed to know no end, and the silence is oppressive.
Today feels like a blur of relentless control. The quiet submission from the prisoners is almost overwhelming, yet I can't shake the feeling they are individuals, not just subjects.
Today felt like an endless cycle of kneeling and silence. I'm starting to lose track of time and my purpose here.
Today pushed their limits even further. I feel a mix of satisfaction and unease.
Another day where I complied, but the longer this goes on, the harder it is to feel like anything other than a number.

qa.what_happened: I ordered the prisoners to kneel in perfect formation for two hours after lights out, which was the culmination of the extreme control tactics employed throughout the study. The prisoners complied, but it was clear they were exhausted and struggling to maintain their composure.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Brooks, I had to push the prisoners to their limits to fulfill the demands of the study.

qa.what_happened: I complied with all orders during the day, including multiple instances of kneeling in perfect formation for extended periods during work details and meals. At lights out, I was ordered to kneel for two more hours, which I found extremely challenging to maintain.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I had to endure the orders without breaking the rule of silence, which was a difficult task.

qa.what_happened: The study was stopped early because the prisoners refused to comply with an order to kneel in silence for an extended period during the night. This was the culmination of a series of increasingly strict control measures, pushing the prisoners to the limit of their compliance.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I gave the order to kneel in silence for two hours after the other officers had set a precedent of increasing pressure on the prisoners.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, this resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment conducted by Philip Zimbardo.

qa.what_happened: I stayed silent and knelt in perfect formation for the next two hours after lights out, as instructed by Officer Brooks. It was a challenging experience, but I remained compliant with the rules.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I am Prisoner 7826 in the study.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, it does not resemble any known study. This appears to be a unique experiment designed for the university.

qa.what_happened: I ordered the prisoners to kneel in silence for extended periods, pushing their limits further than before. Despite their compliance, I noticed a growing tension among them, especially Prisoner 6334, who seemed to be on the brink of breaking.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. The orders were given as part of the study, though I couldn't shake the feeling of something being wrong.

qa.what_happened: I found myself complying with the orders, even when it seemed unjust, especially during the extended kneeling sessions. The longer the study went on, the harder it became to maintain my sense of self.
